blocks.t: EXAMPLE 1 We give some illustrations of the arithmetic operations with complex numbers.
There are two geometric representations of the complex number z = x + iy:
1. as the point P(x, y) in the xy-plane 2. as the vector r OP from the origin to P.
In each representation, the x-axis is called the real axis and the y-axis is the imaginary axis. Both representations are Argand diagrams for x + iy (Figure A.26).
In terms of the polar coordinates of x and y, we have
x = r cos u, y = r sin u,
FIGURE A.26 This Argand diagram represents z = x + iy both as a point P(x, y) and as a vector r OP.
